## Body

Flake diagnosis (F228, #278 merged 9ffc5729):
- Measure first: build test bins once via `just shared-build -- test ... --no-run --message-format=json-render-diagnostics`, copy the executable out of the shared target, run it N times niced (`--exact --test-threads 1` and whole-binary). Add the outcomes to an assert to see the real error. The CAS "flake" was a tmux SIGSEGV, not timing.
- `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/tmux-*.ips` (procLaunch vs crash time) tells you if a server crashed. Never paste that path in PRs/ledger (C21): say "macOS DiagnosticReports".
- CI `server exited unexpectedly` at teardown = kill-server exit 1 while the server goes; postcondition is "no server" (F27 pattern, `list-sessions` fails). Mutation: fake tmux on PATH.
- Poll counts and fixed sleeps are clocks. Drive by state (row landed) and use barriers like `services.delivery.flush()`. PIJ_TEST_TIME_SCALE can't go below 1; inject slowness instead (a SQLite trigger burning CPU on INSERT).

tmux crash + lock (F229, #280, round 2 head c8d2eab2, verdicts pending):
- Two control clients attaching concurrently with setup `destroy-unattached on` SIGSEGV tmux 3.6a (shell repro 12-14/30). In-process threads rarely reproduce; two PROCESSES with plain `tmux -L` (not the logging wrapper) give ~50%.
- Fix: flock `<tap root>/.control-attach-<label>.lock` held attach->sentinel. Round 1 waited (sleep loop on a Tokio worker under the state mutex) and then forked every read for the 5 s backoff -> BLOCKED (R280-001/P280-001). RESTART_BACKOFF caps STARTS, not read forks; fallback costs (1+3N)/0.6 launches/s from the observer.
- Round 2: try_lock once; held -> Query::Busy (read error, no launch), retry next read; refuse only after 5 s (frozen holder). Typed AttachLockHeld error (spawn EAGAIN is also WouldBlock). Probe: 50 ms timer on a current_thread runtime must fire on time.
- A forked child briefly holds a copy of a flock'd fd until exec (CLOEXEC): "taken at once after release" tests need a short retry under parallel tests.
- Open: S280-001 lock file mode follows umask. Upstream tmux draft sent to pm-001, not posted.

Next (F232, after #280 merges): CodexBinder marks rows/locks seen BEFORE probing (codex_bind.rs ~242-265), so an Err (e.g. Busy) is never retried. Fix: unmark the row on a probe Err; keep Seen for real decisions (registration refusal = decision). RED test = minnow's `reviewer_one_busy_probe_is_not_retried_after_release` (diff in pm-001's message). Cost: tick is 5 s; a persistent Err would re-probe (lsof on macOS) every tick -> cap consecutive Err retries per row and say so in the cost row.
